subject: Request: Cross-border exportability matrix & mapping for Redwood (MedSys)
messages:
From: Ankur Patel <ankur.patel@medsys.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: security@medsys.com
Date: 2026-09-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Cross-border data flow details + exportability matrix request

Hi Rachel,

Thanks for the quick intro earlier. MedSys Health is kicking off an internal Transfer Impact Assessment for our planned integration with Redwood. Before our DPIA meeting next week we need two things from you: a) a completed exportability mapping (which fields/processes move outside the EEA/UK and to which destinations), and b) confirmation of the legal mechanisms you rely on (SCCs, DPA addendum, adequacy, etc.).

Specific asks:
- Can you fill our matrix template (attached) or provide an equivalent exportability matrix?
- Do you have an SCCs attestation or standard DPA addendum we can include in our records?
- Example audit/logging evidence showing what audit fields are retained and for how long (a redacted screenshot is fine).
- Any notes if our workloads would be considered PHI under US rules and whether Hosted is acceptable or Private/Dedicated would be required.

Target timeline: we'd like the filled matrix and any attestation drafts by 2026-10-05 so it can go into our DPIA draft.

Thanks,
Ankur
Security & Privacy Lead
MedSys Health

Attachments: medsys_exportability_template.xlsx (attached on our side)
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Ankur Patel <ankur.patel@medsys.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-28T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Cross-border data flow details + exportability matrix request

Hi Ankur — thanks for the clear ask. We're happy to support the DPIA. I've attached an exportability matrix template we've used with other healthcare customers (redwood_exportability_matrix_v1.xlsx) and a small redacted logging snippet to show the kinds of audit fields we keep (sample_logging_snippet.png).

High level:
- Legal mechanisms: we operate under our standard DPA (EU Addendum + SCCs as appropriate) for hosted customers transferring data outside the EEA/UK. We also provide a signed SCCs attestation template we can share for procurement records — I've included a draft (redwood_sccs_attestation_draft.pdf) for your legal team to review.
- Evidence: we cannot provide raw production logs, but we can provide redacted samples and screenshots that demonstrate fields/timestamps retained for audit and troubleshooting.
- HIPAA / PHI: for workloads that contain PHI we recommend our Private or Dedicated deployment options (customer-managed VPC/KMS) — Hosted is generally not appropriate for PHI unless there is an explicit contractual BAA and set of controls agreed; happy to discuss.

I'll coordinate with Marcus (security) to confirm the mapping details and produce a filled copy of your matrix by your 2026-10-05 deadline. Would you prefer the completed matrix returned as an XLSX or a Google Sheet link?

Best,
Rachel Kim
Senior Account Executive — Security & Regulated Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_exportability_matrix_v1.xlsx, sample_logging_snippet.png, redwood_sccs_attestation_draft.pdf
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-28T11:25:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Cross-border data flow details + exportability matrix request

Quick internal note — forwarding Ankur's request. A few things to confirm before we fill the matrix:

1) Scope clarification: is MedSys intending to send PHI (full identifiers + clinical notes) to Redwood Hosted endpoints? If yes, we should propose Private deployment by default. If they only send pseudonymized tokens/metadata, Hosted + SCCs/DPA is usually sufficient.

2) Evidence we can provide: redacted audit log PNG (good), retention schedule (we can provide a table), list of subprocessors and their regions (we maintain that list in our security drive link). We do NOT hand over raw logs or access to customer logs.

3) SCCs & DPA: standard approach is EU SCCs + Redwood DPA addendum. We can supply the signed attestation + link to our published DPA. For UK transfers we rely on the UK Addendum.

4) Timeline: Rachel, we can get a first-pass filled matrix and redacted log sample by 2026-10-02 if you want to send the template back now. I'll review the security language in the attestation draft and propose small clarifications around subprocessors and encryption-in-transit keys.

Action: Rachel — can you attach MedSys's template (Ankur said they attached theirs to the original mail) and I'll start populating columns for data flows + destination regions.

— Marcus
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Hi Ankur,

Thanks for the patience — attached is the completed exportability matrix based on the template you provided (redwood_exportability_matrix_filled.xlsx) and a redacted audit log sample (redacted_audit_log_sample.png). I've also attached the SCCs attestation draft we referenced earlier.

Summary of key points:
- Exportability mapping: most telemetry/usage events are persisted in the EU, but model inference audio/text payloads are routed to our US inference pool for model execution depending on model selection. The attached matrix highlights per-field destinations and temporary cache behavior.
- Legal basis: Hosted transfers are supported under our DPA + SCCs (EU Addendum). For UK subjects we apply the UK Addendum. If MedSys intends to process PHI under US law we recommend Private/Dedicated deployment with customer-managed KMS — we've noted this in the matrix and flagged the relevant rows.
- Evidence: the redacted audit sample shows the timestamp, event type, and request-id fields we retain; we can produce additional redacted samples if your DPIA requires more detail.
- Next steps: if MedSys legal wants edits to the SCCs attestation, send line-item redlines. If you'd like, Marcus and I can run a 30-minute walk-through of the matrix and attestation on Oct 6 — proposed slots: 09:00–09:30 PT or 14:00–14:30 PT.

Best regards,
Rachel Kim
Senior Account Executive — Security & Regulated Accounts
Redwood Inference
